items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I had to go borrow Joe Hall's carnet. He had just bought a new carnet and he didn't use it, you know? I had to go borrow his carnet to go to work that night.

ctx.x: I don't know. That's a year or so before my time. You don't know that? Johnny, you mentioned that one piece that you played first, that they played with Shilling at the ballpark. Which ballpark was it? The Pelican out there? Yeah, when Heinemann Park. They used to call it Heinemann Park. Heinemann Park. Yeah. Out at the end of Tulane? Tulane and Calgary. Same one they call it, Pelican Stadium. Yeah. Where that tourist club is now. That's where you used to go to get your relief during the depression. They used to…

They had circles that week. I'm going to tell you, the last parade I've prayed in my life. The last time I prayed. It was in 1919, they had a car strike. See? And we had to walk from the heritage, we were all human, you see? But we had to hide outside men. So, Shilling got a job. Around 1919. 18 or 19. Because they would have a meet at the old Crescent Theatre. You know the Crescent Theatre? You don't remember the Crescent Theatre? Tulane and Tulane. Tulane, Tulane, yeah. All right. So, Shilling says, come on. I…

Where did you live then, Johnny? Around the prime evening off? Oh, yeah. I lived the whole hallway around the street. You still live on Orleans? No, I don't live around that way anymore. But that was 1990. Bache used to live around that too, didn't he? Bache. Bache, he died, yeah. Yeah, Bache, yeah. I was, when I was, yeah, Sidney, yeah.
